back: The use of machines or computer-controlled systems to do work formerly done by people. Raises output and consistency; may reduce jobs.

front: Benefits and costs of new technology
back: Benefits: lower unit costs, quality, wider markets. Costs: purchase, training, redundancy, obsolescence and dependence on power or the internet.
Competing by lower prices or discounts.
Competing through quality, branding, service, design, convenience and promotion.
If one firm cuts prices or launches a product, rivals may copy it, so the gain may be short-lived and a price war may lower profits for all.
Few suppliers, unique inputs, costly switching, and a buyer that is small or unimportant to the supplier.

front: Ways to reduce dependence on a supplier
back: Use several suppliers, hold inventory, make long-term contracts, build relationships, or integrate backward.
Selling goods and services over the internet: it widens the market and lowers premises costs but needs delivery, payment and security systems.
